Topic: Android will have to let you pick a different AI assistant
Caption Notes: On Android, Google's own assistant gets the best access to your phone. The European Commission has told Google that has to change. Rival assistants like ChatGPT and Claude must get the same hooks, including voice activation and permission to actually do things inside your apps. It's an EU decision, so UK phones may follow along rather than change overnight. Worth knowing before your next upgrade. More plain-English AI news at ainofluff.co.uk.

Topic: ChatGPT's free version just got a lot less limited
Caption Notes: ChatGPT's free plan used to cap how much you could chat in a day. OpenAI has now scrapped that limit for text chats, and swapped in a newer model called GPT-5.6 Luna as the default. In plain terms: if you've been holding back because you kept hitting a wall, you shouldn't anymore. Image and file limits still apply. Worth another look if you tried ChatGPT once and got stuck. Topic: OpenAI's new 'Sign in with ChatGPT' — handy, but know what it shares
Caption Notes: OpenAI has launched 'Sign in with ChatGPT', so you can log into some other apps and sites using your ChatGPT account, a bit like 'Sign in with Google'. It only shares your name, email and photo with the app itself. But OpenAI keeps a record of every app you sign into this way, plus your IP address and device details. Handy for speed. Worth knowing before you use it everywhere. Read more plain-English AI safety at ainofluff.co.uk.
